 JUDGMENT 1.

Aggrieved by the order dated 15.03.2011 passed in KAPAKA/NF/SR-04/2010,
KAPAKA/NF/SR-05/2010 and KAPAKA/NF/SR-06/2010 by the Labour Officer and Commissioner for Workmen Compensation, Hassan Sub- Division, Hassan, the second respondent - Insurance Company therein has preferred these appeals.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Commissioner.

3. The case of the petitioners is that they were working as loaders with the first respondent and that the first respondent owned a tractor bearing registration No.KA-46-T-372 and a trailer bearing registration No.KA-46-T-373 and that they were duly insured with the second respondent - Insurance Company.
The first respondent was permitted to use the tractor and trailer for agriculture and forestry purposes.

In the course of their employment, they were carrying wooden logs for the purpose of constructing a shed and that on 20.07.2009 at about 8.15 p.m. in the night, the driver of the tractor drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and the trailer turtled near Nehru Circle,
Belur Town and because of which, the petitioners fell down and some of the wooden logs fell on them and because of which, they sustained grievous injuries.

Hence, they preferred a claim petition before the Labour Officer and Workmen's Compensation Commissioner (hereinafter referred to as 'Commissioner' for short)
4.

The Commissioner based on the pleadings and evidence let- in has awarded a compensation of Rs.4,42,008/-, Rs.79,693/- and Rs.97,603/- along with interest at the rate of 12% per annum as per the provisions of the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923.

5. Aggrieved by the same, the second respondent - Insurance Company on the ground that the petitioners were not the employees of first respondent and even otherwise, the petitioners were not permitted to travel in the trailer and the Insurance Company is not liable to compensate them in case of accident and even otherwise in the first petition, the compensation awarded is on the higher side has preferred these appeals.
6. The learned advocate for respondent Nos.1 and 2 justify the impugned order and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

sentences.text:
Based on the grounds made out in the appeals, this Court has framed the following substantial questions of law:-
In MFA.No.4934/2011:
1. Whether under the given facts and circumstances of the case, when the first respondent (petitioner before the Commissioner) has not produced any documentary evidence to prove that he was an employee of second respondent, the Commissioner was correct in holding that he was an employee of second respondent (first respondent before the Commissioner)?
2. When it is established that there was no place to travel in the trailer and the first respondent (petitioner before the Commissioner) traveled in the trailer, can the Insurance Company absolve itself from the liability?
3.
Whether the Commissioner was correct in awarding compensation based on functional disability rather than the actual physical disability of the first respondent (petitioner before the Commissioner)?

In MFA.No.4932/2011 & MFA.No.4933/2011:
1. Whether under the given facts and circumstances of the case when the first respondent (petitioner before the Commissioner) has not produced any documentary evidence to prove that he was an employee of second respondent, the Commissioner was correct in holding that he was an employee of second respondent (first respondent before the Commissioner)?

2. When it is established that there was no place to travel in the trailer and the first respondent (petitioner before the Commissioner) traveled in the trailer, can the Insurance Company absolve itself from its liability?
8. The petitioners in their claim statement before the Commissioner and in their affidavit evidence have pleaded that they have been employees of the first respondent - Employer.
The first respondent has not denied this fact and in the course of the arguments before this Court has admitted this fact.

Further, immediately after the accident, FIR has been registered and after due investigation, charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the tractor and both in FIR and in charge sheet, it is recorded that the petitioners were employees of the first respondent and the contention of the petitioners to this effect has not been impeached in the cross-examination.
Though, the Insurance Company has taken a contention to the contrary, for the aforementioned reasons, it has to be held that the petitioners were employees of the first respondent.
No where it is envisaged in law that employment has to be proved only by documentary evidence.
Hence, the first substantial question of law has to be answered against the Insurance Company and it has to be held that the petitioners were employees of first respondent.
Further, based on evidence let in, it also has to be held that they suffered injury in the course of employment.

sentences.text: In respect of second substantial question of law, the petitioners were traveling in a trailer attached to the tractor.
The tractor itself is not a goods vehicle.
However, when the trailer is attached to the tractor, the trailer becomes a goods vehicle.

Thus, any injury to the owner of the goods traveling in the trailer or the authorized representative or employee of the owner traveling in the trailer along with the goods gets covered by the insurance.

However, in the instant case, the question to be decided is what happens when a person travels in the trailer when there is no place to sit in the same and it meets with an accident and the person is injured.

In the instant case, the evidence of PW-1 in MFA.No.4934/2011, clearly establishes that the trailer was filled to the brim with wooden logs and the said logs were tied with a rope and though there was no place to sit in the trailer, the petitioners sat on the wooden logs holding the rope as their only support.

10. Section 146(1) reads as under:
Necessity for Insurance against third party risks:
- 10 - (1) No person shall use, except as a passenger, or cause or allow any other person to use, a motor vehicle in a public place, unless there is in force, in relation to the use of the vehicle by that person or that other person, as the case may be, a policy of insurance complying with the requirements of this Chapter:
xxx Section 147(1) reads as under:
Requirement of policies and limit of liability (1) In order to comply with the requirements of this Chapter, a policy of insurance must be a policy which- (a) is issued by a person who is an authorized insurer; and (b) insures the person or classes of persons specified in the policy to the extent specified in sub-section(2)-
(i) against any liability which may be incurred by him in respect of the death of or bodily injury to any person including owner of the goods or his authorized representative carried in the motor vehicle or damage to any property of a third party caused by or arising out of the use of the motor vehicle in a public place;
(ii) against the death of or bodily injury to any passenger of a transport vehicle,
except gratuitous passengers of a goods vehicle, caused by or arising out of the use of the motor vehicle in a public place.

6 (i) to cover liability in respect of the death, arising out of and in the course of his employment, of the employee of a person insured by the policy or in respect of bodily injury - 11 - sustained by such an employee arising out of and in the course of his employment other than a liability arising under the Workmen's compensation Act, 1923 (8 of 1923), in respect of the death of,
or bodily injury to, any such employee- (a) engaged in driving the vehicle, or (b) if it is a public service vehicle engaged as a conductor of the vehicle or in examining tickets on the vehicle, or (c) if it is a goods carriage, being carried in the vehicle, or (ii) to cover any contractual liability".

sentences.text: Thus, the reading of the above provisions makes it clear that the employee of an owner of the goods vehicle travelling in the said vehicle in the course of employment and the vehicle being used for the purpose it is intended to be used in law, then in that event, any injury to the said employee is covered.

12. However, it is contended by the learned Advocate for the Insurance Company that in the instant case, the Insurance Company is not liable as there was no place for the injured person to travel in the goods vehicle and the injured has put himself at risk by travelling in the vehicle when there was no place to travel and the Insurance Company is not liable to compensate the injured.

. Per contra, learned advocate for the owner contends that as per the decision of the Division Bench of this Court in Branch Manager New India Assurance Co., Ltd Vs. Mallamma reported in LAWS(KAR)-2009-3-43 and in the decision of NATIONAL INSURANCE CO., LTD VS. SRI MARUTHI AND ORS., reported ILR 2011 KAR 4139, the Insurance Company is liable to compensate the injured.

sentences.text:
Paragraph No.8 of Mallamma's case reads as under:
"(8) The gist of the proviso to Sec.147(1) mandates that the risk of the employee in a goods carriage should be statutorily covered.
The expression 'being carried in the vehicle' need not be construed rigidly and strictly, if done, it would defeat the very object and purpose of legislative welfare policy.
In the case of goods vehicle the loading and unloading of goods is an integral part of the transport activity.

The contention that insurer would become liable only when the employee sustains death/injury while travelling in the The New India Assurance Co.Ltd vs Sri Salim Pasha @ Salim on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12426231/
7 vehicle would be an absurd proposition.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co.Ltd vs Sri Salim Pasha @ Salim
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since, the loading and unloading forms an integral and dominant purpose of the transport activity, the risk of the workmen attending to loading and unloading should not be excluded by rigid interpretation.

In that view, we hold that the expression 'being carried in the vehicle' would also include the activity of loading and unloading and not necessarily restricted to the situations where the - 13 - workmen is an inmate of the vehicle at the time of the accident.
Hence, the accident in question is in the course of and out of employment and in the use of motor vehicle.
The insurer cannot avoid the liability."

Paragraph No.31 of Maruthi's case reads as under:
31.

By reading Sections 147 and 149, it is clear that the Legislative intent was that the insurer has to compulsorily cover all the risks arising out of and use of motor vehicle and the liability of the insurer is co-extensive with that of insured.
However, this is subject to the limitations envisaged under Section 147(1)( b).

It is also clear that the coolies who are employees carried in a goods vehicle are to be compulsorily covered under Section 147(1)(b).
14.

The observations of this Court in the aforesaid judgments makes it clear that the legislative intent is that the insurer has to compulsorily cover all the risks arising out of and use of motor vehicle and the liability of insurer is co-extensive with that of insured.
The insurer can escape liability only if it can bring its case within the exempted provisions of Motor Vehicles Act.

No doubt,
in the instant case, the petitioners and the owner have taken a risk in making the petitioners travel in the trailer when there was no place to sit.
However, this does not come under any of the exemption in Section 149 of the Motor - 14 - Vehicles Act or any other provisions.
There is no clause in the insurance policy that such an act of the owner of the injured would absolve the Insurance Company from its liability.
15. Thus, the second substantial question of law also has to be held against the Insurance Company and it has to be held that the Insurance Company is liable to compensate the petitioners.
16. In respect of third substantial question of law in MFA.No.4934/2011, the petitioner is a loader and a coolie.
Because of his injury, he has no control over his bladder and passing of urine.

Taking this particular fact into consideration, based on the evidence let in, the Commissioner has come to the conclusion that the petitioner has suffered 100% functional disability and has determined the compensation.
I do not see any error in the same.
Hence, the third substantial question of law in MFA.No.4934/2011 is also held against the Insurance Company.
